title: CLT Panel Properties Calculator
tagline: Structural analysis tool for Cross Laminated Timber panels per Eurocode 5
description: An OOP JavaScript calculator that implements two structural engineering methods Shear Analogy and Gamma Method (Eurocode 5)  to analyze Cross Laminated Timber (CLT) panel properties. Converts a previously Excel-based engineering model into an interactive, browser-based tool.
fullDescription:
Problem: Structural engineers evaluating CLT panels relied on a rigid Excel-based model to calculate panel properties using Shear Analogy and Gamma Method (Eurocode 5). This made the workflow error-prone, hard to validate, and difficult to extend to new layer configurations.

Solution: Built a web-based calculator from scratch in vanilla JavaScript using OOP principles, after a 3-day intensive research process into a completely new engineering domain (structural timber analysis) I had no prior background in. Designed decoupled layer/layup classes to represent CLT panel composition, each with custom validation rules specific to the constraints of each calculation method. The tool independently re-derives and validates the same complex calculations as the original Excel model.

Role: Sole developer — researched the domain (Eurocode 5 structural formulas), designed the OOP architecture, and implemented both calculation methods end-to-end.

Outcome: A working calculator that reproduces and validates complex structural engineering calculations previously locked in a spreadsheet, submitted as a technical assessment and demonstrating the ability to acquire deep domain knowledge in an unfamiliar field under time constraint.

tools.desc: Core language used to implement the calculator logic using object-oriented design, with no external framework dependency.

tools.title: Eurocode 5 Standards
tools.desc: Structural engineering standard defining the Shear Analogy and Gamma Method formulas implemented in the calculator.

techBreakdown.name: Vanilla JS + OOP
techBreakdown.reason: Chosen to keep the calculation engine framework-agnostic and to model panel/layer relationships cleanly through class-based structures, mirroring how engineers conceptually break down CLT layups.

techBreakdown.name: Decoupled Layer/Layup Classes
techBreakdown.reason: Separating layer and layup logic allowed each calculation method's specific constraints to be validated independently, preventing cross-method configuration errors.

challenges.title: Learning a New Engineering Domain Under Time Pressure
challenges.description: Had no prior background in structural timber engineering. Had to research Shear Analogy and Gamma Method from Eurocode 5 documentation, understand the underlying physics, and translate that into correct, testable code within a 3-day window.

challenges.title: Validating Against an Existing Excel Model
challenges.description: The calculator's outputs needed to match the original spreadsheet's results exactly. This required independently re-deriving the formulas rather than blindly porting spreadsheet logic, catching and correcting a discrepancy in the process.

challenges.title: Method-Specific Layer Constraints
challenges.description: Shear Analogy and Gamma Method impose different validity rules on layer configuration (e.g. layer count, orientation). Designing a class structure flexible enough to enforce both methods' constraints without duplicating logic was a key architectural decision.

Outcome: Delivered a functional MVP platform that handles event creation, discovery, and registration with a clean separation between organizer and attendee experiences.

Outcome: Delivered a complete booking platform that allows users to browse properties on an interactive map, check availability, and complete bookings — all within a seamless, responsive interface.

challenges.title: Complex Booking State Management
challenges.description: The multi-step booking flow (property selection → date picker → guest info → payment) required tracking partial data across steps without losing progress. Managed this with Redux Thunk middleware — each step dispatches async actions that validate and persist intermediate state, with a booking slice that resets on completion or cancellation.

challenges.title: Map Integration with Property Data

Solved by debouncing map move events and dispatching a Redux action that updates both the marker layer and the property list simultaneously.
